claims.text: The feedstock is a cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder suitable for laser powder bed fusion.
The intervention is build-plate preheating to approximately 400°C during laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-plate preheating reduces thermal gradients during deposition and solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients suppress solute partitioning and compositional segregation.
Preheating lowers dislocation stress concentrations.
Preheating moderates the cooling rate.
A moderated cooling rate diminishes abrupt thermal contraction and thereby reduces residual stress.
The controlled thermal environment encourages more uniform grain growth.
The controlled thermal environment reduces defect nucleation.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will have a lower density of microstructural defects than specimens produced without preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will have lower residual stresses than specimens produced without preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will exhibit increased tensile yield strength relative to specimens produced without preheating.
The relevant baseline is AlCrFeNiSi fabricated by laser powder bed fusion without build-plate preheating.
The comparison is intended to hold scanning speed, energy density, and processing atmosphere constant.
The hypothesis is restricted to laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi with a preheat temperature near 400°C and otherwise identical laser parameters.
Changing the preheat temperature or laser parameters may produce different outcomes.
Literature supports residual-stress reduction by preheating in similar material systems.
The magnitude of mechanical improvement and the optimal preheat temperature for AlCrFeNiSi are not established.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing preheated and non-preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens using tensile testing, residual-stress measurement, and microstructural characterization.
Failure to obtain statistically significant mechanical improvement together with reduced residual stress and reduced segregation or defect evidence would falsify the hypothesis.
